request: A vacation calendar based on holidays and vacation requests, viewable for the whole organization, for several teams, or for specific people, drawn as a horizontal timeline where each row is a member and each column is a day. Holidays follow a country a manager states on the member, falling back to a country stated on the organization; the phone country code is not a source.
shardDecision: read myself, no shards dispatched. The slice offered one shard per member across 1,487 lines, and the pass is a change sweep over a 10-finding repair, not a full reading — the diff is 369 insertions across four files. Every finding I had to settle is cross-file by construction: R1 is a case in cases.md judged against REQ-01-026/027/029/040 in the behaviour file and acceptance criterion 8; R2 is the DS-gaps table in contracts.md judged against the mock and packages/ds tokens at once; and the fixer's declared `subtraction` deleted three passages from the behaviour file on the claim that each survives elsewhere, which can only be checked by holding the behaviour file and the contracts together. A per-file split would have handed each shard the half of every question it cannot answer, and the subtraction check — the highest-risk part of this repair — would have been invisible to every shard. Code read to settle the claims the repair newly introduced: apps/api/src/holidays/holidays.service.ts (scope=mine gating at :86-105), apps/api/src/holidays/holidays.controller.ts (no RequireCapability), packages/ds/src/tokens/spacing.css, and the mock's full colour-literal sweep.
sweeps: Range reconstruction. `git diff 0f20da7..HEAD` touches one file, `.workflow/refine/time-off-01.loop.json`, and the slice reported 'the repair touched no bundle file, which is itself the finding'. That reading is wrong: `git log` shows 0f20da7 is itself the commit titled 'refine(time-off-01): round 1 fix spec-fixer-minimal — 5 fixed, 5 decided, 0 left', and `git show --stat` on it lists all four bundle files. The repair is the base of the given range, not something inside it. I judged the actual repair diff, bfd7e4c..0f20da7, which is what round 1's ledger entry records as head→commit. Recorded as N1 below, addressed to the harness and not to the document.

Blocker R1 (S-37, TC-01-INT-12). Repaired and correct. The case now takes two reads and answers each. First read: A stated `US` → `US`; B stated `PL` → `PL`; C stated nothing → `PL` by the organization fallback; D stated `XX`, which REQ-01-027 skips → `PL`. Second read, organization country cleared: A and B unchanged, C and D `null` under REQ-01-040, carrying only the global holiday under REQ-01-029. The identical-inputs-two-answers defect is gone, because C and D now differ in the first read by D's unusable `XX` and agree in the second, which is what the requirements say must happen. Covers gained REQ-01-027 and REQ-01-040 and the Asserts line carries both 200s. Acceptance criterion 8 still names TC-01-UNIT-01 and TC-01-INT-12 and now genuinely has an integration observer for its `null` branch.

Blocker R2 (S-22, DS gaps). Repaired and correct, and the exhaustive claim is now true rather than merely narrower. The Screens section names `ToggleButton` for the three `calendar-scope-*` and three `calendar-window-*` segments and adds 'The calendar draws no segmented control of its own'; the Keyboard row attributes the roving tabindex to that component. The mock follows: `.seg.on` takes `var(--shadow-toggle-active)` in place of `rgba(0,0,0,.12)`, `.sw` takes `var(--radius-s)` in place of 3px, `.band` takes `var(--space-10)` in place of 30px, and the 3px side margin carries an `@literal` comment with its reason. A third DS-gaps row records the two sub-`--space-1` measures. I verified the first row's rewritten claim, 'no colour on this screen is written as a literal', by grepping the whole mock for `rgba(`, `rgb(` and hex: zero matches — the only colour values are the three `oklch()` names in the page's own `:root`, which is exactly what that row sanctions. The mock's closing paragraph correctly dropped its old and false 'Everything else on the page is an existing token' rather than replacing it with a second over-claim.

The DS-gaps third row's precision, checked rather than assumed. The row says the 3px hatch stripe is 'in the legend swatch'. That is exact: `.sw.pending` (mock :97) is `0 3px, transparent 3px 6px`, while `.band.pending` (mock :164-165) is `0 4px, transparent 4px 8px` — a different stripe that is not below `--space-1`. The fixer distinguished the two rather than collapsing them, which the row it wrote would have gotten wrong if it had.

The fixer's `subtraction` — the highest-risk part of this repair, since it deletes text on a claim that the content survives elsewhere. All three verified. (1) The Summary's dropped 'The later time-off policy catalogue lands by giving that field more values' is carried by REQ-01-025's Decided, 'the one field added ahead of its need, so the policy catalogue lands by adding values', and the Summary now cites REQ-01-025 by id. (2) The dropped capability sentence survives verbatim at contracts :207: 'Neither country write adds a capability: `ManageHolidays` and `edit-detail` already grant exactly the admin and manager who set them.' (3) REQ-01-045's dropped PII clause is carried by the Security section's 'No PII is read or emitted' bullet, which states the `MemberProfile.country` / `ViewMemberProfilePii` distinction in full. Nothing was subtracted into nowhere.

Today holidays.service.ts:103 resolves from `account?.phoneCountryCode`; the case gives the member a `BY` phone country and a `PL` holiday, so the shipped code returns the global holiday alone and fails the case, while the adopted chain returns both on both reads. Contradiction sweep across the bundle, with attention to what the repair could have broken. The new `holidays[]` window clause agrees with TC-01-INT-13 (both its holidays are inside the window) and with Edge case 13. The new first-failure ordering is consistent: its worked example, inverted plus scope `everyone`, resolves to rule 3 `rangeInverted` before rule 5 `scopeInvalid`, and no case in the file sends two invalid inputs at once, so nothing existing is contradicted; rules 5 and 8 are server-only and 8 is only reachable after 3 and 5 pass, so the stated order is satisfiable. The new Routes row and front-matter entry agree. `TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES.memberCountryDefaultOption` is declared once in the Error Messages table and referenced by the Screens paragraph and TC-01-E2E-08. The out-of-sequence placement of TC-01-INT-29 and of several REQ ids (REQ-01-040 after 026, REQ-01-041 after 009) is the file's established thematic house style, not drift.

spec-lint re-run on the current tree: clean — 50 requirements, 41 cases, 6 routes, 14 messages, 26 testids. This matches the fixer's reported count exactly and reconciles with the judge's pre-repair 40/5/13 plus the one case, one route and one message the repair added.

findings.claim: Outside the admission register and addressed to the harness, not to the document — no edit to the spec is being asked for. The range this pass was given, `0f20da7..HEAD`, excludes the repair it was asked to judge, because 0f20da7 is the repair commit itself rather than the commit before it. `scripts/spec-slice.mjs --since 0f20da7` therefore reported 'nothing — the repair touched no bundle file, which is itself the finding', which is false and is the most expensive kind of false: taken at face value it convicts a fixer that did its work, and it hides all 369 lines of the change from the sweep that is supposed to read them. The round-1 ledger entry records `head: bfd7e4c` and `commit: 0f20da7`, so the diff a change pass wants is `head..commit`, not `commit..HEAD`. I judged bfd7e4c..0f20da7 and the verdict above is against that diff.

witness.detail: `git log --oneline 0f20da7..HEAD` → one commit, '2ba950c refine(time-off-01): round 2 T0 spec-lint — clean', touching only .workflow/refine/time-off-01.loop.json. `git show --stat 0f20da7` → '0f20da7 refine(time-off-01): round 1 fix spec-fixer-minimal — 5 fixed, 5 decided, 0 left', listing 01-vacation-calendar.cases.md (+56/-...), .contracts.md (+64), .md (+18), .mock.html (+17). `git status --porcelain` shows no modification to any specs/time-off path, so the working tree adds nothing either. Ledger rounds[0]: head bfd7e4c7ecb5a16c7eb25bf4c555f22de4038102, commit 0f20da7ff6d85ad6357781d576d26bd3ee32d5dd.

findings.suggestedFix: Where a change pass computes its `--since`, pass the prior round's `head` rather than its `commit` — the ledger already stores both. Failing that, `spec-slice.mjs` should not report an empty bundle diff as a finding when the given base is itself a commit that touched the bundle; that condition is detectable with one `git show --stat` on the base and is the difference between 'the fixer did nothing' and 'you were handed the wrong end of the range'.
